newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala says coffee stocks at 500,000 60-kg bags.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala says coffee stocks at 500,000 60-kg bags.

text.p: Guatemala has exportable coffee stocks of around 500,000 60-kg bags remaining from the 1996-1997 coffee harvest, the National Coffee Association (Anacafe) said on Wednesday.

Through April 15, Guatemala had exported 3,017,530 60-kilo sacks of coffee, Anacafe President Julio Arrivillaga told Reuters. He said total exports for the harvest should reach 3.5 to 3.6 million 60-kilo bags, including other leftover stocks.

"Almost everything is gone. Once April is finished, in May the exports will really come down, there won't be any more coffee to ship," Anacafe president Julio Arrivillaga told Reuters. Guatemala's harvest has virtually ended, with only a nominal amount of beans still to be picked.
Exports during the 1995-1996 harvest were 3.68 million bags, he said.

Arrivillaga said there is no way to know for sure how much had already been sold on the futures market. "I'm speculating but we do believe that it is practically all contracted. There could still be changes," he said.
